option.name: --quiet

option.name: --raw
tip: Generate the diff in raw format.

option.name: --rename-empty

option.name: --rotate-to
tip: Move the files before the named <file> to the end of the output.

option.name: --shortstat

option.name: --skip-to

option.name: --stat-graph-width
tip: Limit the width of the graph part in --stat output.

option.name: --stat-width

tip: Highlight errors in new lines.

option.name: --always

option.name: --anchored
tip: Generate a diff using the "anchored diff" algorithm.

option.name: --binary
tip: In addition to --full-index, output a binary diff that can be applied with git-apply.
Implies --patch.

option.name: --cc

option.name: --check
tip: Warn if changes introduce conflict markers or whitespace errors.
What are considered whitespace errors is controlled by core.whitespace configuration.

option.name: --color
tip: Show colored diff. --color (i.e. without =<when>) is the same as --color=always.

next.name: always
tip: Always use colors.

next.name: auto
tip: Use colors if terminal supports them.

next.name: never
tip: Never use colors.

option.name: --color-moved
tip: Moved lines of code are colored differently. The <mode> defaults to no if the option is not given and to zebra if the option with no mode is given.

option.name: --color-moved-ws
tip: This configures how whitespace is ignored when performing the move detection for --color-moved.
These modes can be given as a comma separated list.

option.name: --color-words
tip: Equivalent to --word-diff=color plus (if a regex was specified) --word-diff-regex=<regex>.

option.name: --combined-all-paths
tip: This flag causes combined diffs (used for merge commits) to list the name of the file from all parents.

tip: Format to use for the commit list in format-patch.

tip: Use Myers diff algorithm (default).

tip: Use patience diff algorithm.

option.name: --dirstat
tip: Output the distribution of relative amount of changes for each sub-directory.

option.name: --dirstat-by-file
tip: Synonym for --dirstat=files,<param>,....

option.name: --dst-prefix
tip: Show the given destination <prefix> instead of "b/".

option.name: --exit-code
tip: Make the program exit with codes similar to diff(1). That is, it exits with 1 if there were differences and 0 means no differences.

option.name: --expand-tabs
tip: Perform a tab expansion (replace each tab with enough spaces to fill to the next display column that is a multiple of <n>) in the log message before showing it in the output.
--expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=8, and --no-expand-tabs is a short-hand for --expand-tabs=0, which disables tab expansion.

option.name: --ext-diff
tip: Allow an external diff helper to be executed.
If you set an external diff driver with gitattributes(5), you need to use this option with git-log(1) and friends.

option.name: --find-copies-harder
tip: For performance reasons, by default, -C option finds copies only if the original file of the copy was modified in the same changeset.
This flag makes the command inspect unmodified files as candidates for copies.

option.name: --find-object
tip: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified object.
Similar to -S, just the argument is different in that it doesn't search for a specific string but for a specific object id.

tip: Pretty-print the contents of the commit logs in a given format, where <format> can be one of oneline, short, medium, full, fuller, reference, email, raw, format:<string> and tformat:<string>.

option.name: --full-index
tip: Instead of the first handful of characters, show the full pre- and post-image blob object names on the "index" line when generating patch format output.

option.name: --histogram
tip: Generate a diff using the "histogram diff" algorithm.

option.name: --ignore-space-at-eol
tip: Ignore changes in whitespace at EOL.

option.name: --ignore-submodules
tip: Ignore changes to submodules in the diff generation. all is the default.

option.name: --indent-heuristic
tip: Enable the heuristic that shifts diff hunk boundaries to make patches easier to read. This is the default.

option.name: --inter-hunk-context
tip: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other.
Defaults to diff.interHunkContext or 0 if the config option is unset.

tip: Display the full sha1s in the output listing rather than abbreviating them.

tip: Turn off colored diff. It is the same as --color=never.

tip: Turn off move detection. This can be used to override configuration settings. It is the same as --color-moved=no.

option.name: --export-marks

option.name: --bisect-all

option.name: --bisect-vars

option.name: --boundary

option.name: --branches

option.name: --cherry

option.name: --cherry-mark
tip: Like --cherry-pick but mark equivalent commits with = rather than omitting them, and inequivalent ones with +.

option.name: --cherry-pick
tip: Omit any commit that introduces the same change as another commit on the "other side" when the set of commits are limited with symmetric difference.

option.name: --children
tip: Print also the children of the commit (in the form "commit child...").

option.name: --commit-header
tip: Overrides a previous --no-commit-header.

option.name: --commit-list-format
tip: Format to use for the commit list in format-patch.

option.name: --count
tip: Print a number stating how many commits would have been listed, and suppress all other output.
When used together with --left-right, instead print the counts for left and right commits, separated by a tab.

option.name: --date
tip: Only takes effect for dates shown in human-readable format, such as when using --pretty.
log.date config variable sets a default value for the log command's --date option.

option.name: --date-order
tip: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the commit timestamp order.

option.name: --decorate
tip: Print out references (branch and tag names) that point at the shown commits.

option.name: --dense
tip: Only the selected commits are shown, plus some to have a meaningful history.

option.name: --disk-usage
tip: Suppress normal output; instead, print the sum of the bytes used for on-disk storage by the selected commits or objects.
This is equivalent to piping the output into git cat-file --batch-check='%(objectsize:disk)', except that it runs much faster.

option.name: --do-walk
tip: Overrides a previous --no-walk.

option.name: --encoding
tip: Commit objects record the character encoding used for the log message in their encoding header; this option can be used to tell the command to re-code the commit log message in the encoding specified by the option value.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Do not include refs matching <glob-pattern> that the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob would otherwise consider.
Repetitions of this option accumulate exclusion patterns.

option.name: --exclude-first-parent-only
tip: When finding commits to exclude (with a ^), follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit.

option.name: --exclude-hidden

option.name: --expand-tabs

option.name: --filter-print-omitted
tip: Only useful with --filter=; prints a list of the objects omitted by the filter.

option.name: --filter-provided-objects

Only useful with --filter=.

option.name: --first-parent

option.name: --full-history
tip: Same as the default mode, but does not prune some history.

option.name: --glob

option.name: --graph

option.name: --graph-lane-limit

option.name: --grep

option.name: --grep-reflog

tip: Add a new working tree to the current repository.

option.name: --checkout
tip: Populate the new working tree.

option.name: --detach
tip: Detach HEAD at the named commit.

option.name: --force
tip: Checkout <branch> even if already checked out in other worktree.

option.name: --guess-remote
tip: Try to match the new branch name with a remote-tracking branch.

option.name: --lock
tip: Keep the new working tree locked.

option.name: --orphan
tip: Create an unborn branch.

option.name: --quiet
tip: Suppress progress reporting.

option.name: --reason
tip: Reason for locking the worktree.

option.name: --relative-paths
tip: Use relative paths for worktrees.

option.name: --track
tip: Set up tracking mode (see git-branch).

option.name: -b
tip: Create a new branch.

option.name: -B
tip: Create or reset a branch.

next.name: list
tip: List all working trees in the current repository.

option.name: --expire
tip: Add 'prunable' annotation to worktrees older than <time>.

option.name: --porcelain
tip: Give the output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Show extended annotations and reasons, if available.

option.name: -z
tip: Terminate records with a NUL character.

next.name: lock
tip: Lock the current working tree to prevent concurrent access.

option.name: --reason
tip: Reason for locking the worktree.

next.name: move
tip: Move or rename a working tree in the current repository.

option.name: --force
tip: Force move even if the worktree is dirty or locked.

option.name: --relative-paths
tip: Use relative paths for worktrees.

next.name: prune
tip: Remove stale working tree administrative files.

option.name: --dry-run
tip: Do not remove, show only.

option.name: --expire
tip: Expire working trees older than <time>.

option.name: --verbose
tip: Report pruned working trees.

next.name: remove
tip: Remove a working tree from the current repository.

option.name: --force
tip: Force removal even if the worktree is dirty or locked.

next.name: repair
tip: Repair worktree administrative files in the given paths, or the default working tree.

option.name: --relative-paths
tip: Use relative paths for worktrees.

next.name: unlock
tip: Unlock the current working tree to allow concurrent access.

next.name: write-tree
tip: Create a tree object from the current index.

option.name: --attr-source
tip: Read gitattributes from <tree-ish> instead of the worktree.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_ATTR_SOURCE environment variable.

option.name: --bare
tip: Treat the repository as a bare repository.
If GIT_DIR environment is not set, it is set to the current working directory.

option.name: --config-env
tip: Like -c <name>=<value>, but take the configuration value from the environment variable <envvar> instead of (or in addition to) the configuration file.
The environment variable is overridden by the configuration given via -c.

option.name: --exec-path
tip: Path to wherever your core Git programs are installed.
This can also be controlled by setting the GIT_EXEC_PATH environment variable.
If no path is given, git will print the current setting and then exit.

option.name: --git-dir
tip: Set the path to the repository (".git" directory).
This can also be controlled by setting the GIT_DIR environment variable.
It can be an absolute path or relative path to current working directory.

option.name: --glob-pathspecs
tip: Add "glob" magic to all pathspec.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS environment variable to 1.
Disabling globbing on individual pathspecs can be done using pathspec magic ":(literal)"

option.name: --html-path
tip: Print the path, without trailing slash, where Git's HTML documentation is installed and exit.

option.name: --icase-pathspecs
tip: Add "icase" magic to all pathspec.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS environment variable to 1.

option.name: --info-path
tip: Print the path where the Info files documenting this version of Git are installed and exit.

option.name: --list-cmds
tip: List commands by group.
This is an internal/experimental option and may change or be removed in the future.

option.name: --literal-pathspecs
tip: Treat pathspecs literally (i.e. no globbing, no pathspec magic).
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS environment variable to 1.

option.name: --man-path
tip: Print the manpath for the man pages for this version of Git and exit.

option.name: --namespace
tip: Set the Git namespace.
Equivalent to setting the GIT_NAMESPACE environment variable.

option.name: --no-advice
tip: Disable all advice hints from being printed.

option.name: --no-lazy-fetch
tip: Do not fetch missing objects from the promisor remote on demand.
Useful together with git cat-file -e <object> to see if the object is locally available.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH environment variable to 1.

option.name: --no-optional-locks
tip: Do not perform optional operations that require locks.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS to 0.

option.name: --no-pager
tip: Do not pipe Git output into a pager.

option.name: --no-replace-objects
tip: Do not use replacement refs to replace Git objects.
This is equivalent to exporting the GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS environment variable with any value.

option.name: --noglob-pathspecs
tip: Add "literal" magic to all pathspec.
This is equivalent to setting the GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS environment variable to 1.
Enabling globbing on individual pathspecs can be done using pathspec magic ":(glob)"

option.name: --paginate
tip: Pipe all output into less (or if set, $PAGER) if standard output is a terminal.
This overrides the pager.<cmd> configuration options.

option.name: --version
tip: Prints the Git suite version that the git program came from.
If --help is also given, it takes precedence over --version.

option.name: --work-tree
tip: Set the path to the working tree. It can be an absolute path or a path relative to the current working directory.
This can also be controlled by setting the GIT_WORK_TREE environment variable and the core.worktree configuration variable

option.name: -c
tip: Pass a configuration parameter to the command. The value given will override values from configuration files.
The <name> is expected in the same format as listed by git config (subkeys separated by dots).

option.name: -C
tip: Run as if git was started in <path> instead of the current working directory.
If <path> is present but empty, e.g. -C "", then the current working directory is left unchanged.

global_option.name: --help
tip: Prints the synopsis and a list of the most commonly used commands.
If the option --all or -a is given then all available commands are printed.
If a Git command is named this option will bring up the manual page for that command.

config.name: max_commit
tip: The maximum number that can be parsed for a project commit by the hooks. Default to <@Magenta>30<@Blue>.
If it is <@Magenta>-1<@Blue>, all commits will be parsed, which may affect the loading speed.
